title: Two-Step Story Problem Task Cards
subject: Mathematics
standard: NC.3.OA.8 - Solve two-step word problems using addition, subtraction, and multiplication, representing problems with equations containing a symbol for the unknown.
source: North Carolina Department of Public Instruction, Mathematics Standards Vertical Progression: https://www.dpi.nc.gov/documents/publications/catalog/ma196-vertical-progression-math/open; NC Check-Ins 2.0 Mathematics Specifications: https://www.dpi.nc.gov/documents/accountability/testing/nc-checkin/nc-check-ins-20-mathematics-grades-3-8-specifications (accessed September 14, 2026).
focus: Solve and represent two-step problems, then check whether answers are reasonable.
qs: A class packs 6 boxes with 8 markers each, then gives away 15 markers. How many remain?
Mia reads 24 pages Monday and 18 Tuesday. Her book has 70 pages. How many remain?
Four teams collect 9 cans each and then collect 17 more. Total?
A garden has 7 rows with 9 plants each. Three plants in each row do not bloom. How many plants bloom?
A store had 85 notebooks, sold 29, then received 40. How many now?
Five buses carry 7 students each. Twelve more arrive by car. Total?
Write an equation for 9 bags of 4 apples with 11 apples eaten.
A player earns 8 points in each of 3 rounds and loses 5 penalty points. Score?
Lena has $50, buys two games at $14 each. Money left?
A baker makes 72 rolls and sells 4 trays with 8 rolls each. How many rolls remain?
Choose the first operation: 6 shelves hold 5 books each; 9 are borrowed.
Create a two-step problem with answer 26.
Answers vary; both operations and equation required.
A student says 4 x 9 - 7 = 29. Is the student correct?
Represent: 45 stickers shared among 5 students, then each gets 2 more.

title: Multi-Digit Multiplication Warm-Up Week
subject: Mathematics
standard: NC.5.NBT.5 - Demonstrate fluency with multiplication of whole numbers up to three digits by two digits using the standard algorithm.
source: North Carolina Department of Public Instruction, Mathematics Standards Vertical Progression: https://www.dpi.nc.gov/documents/publications/catalog/ma196-vertical-progression-math/open; NC Check-Ins 2.0 Mathematics Specifications: https://www.dpi.nc.gov/documents/accountability/testing/nc-checkin/nc-check-ins-20-mathematics-grades-3-8-specifications (accessed September 14, 2026).
focus: Build accurate, fluent standard-algorithm multiplication with estimation and error analysis.
qs: A printer makes 125 pages per minute for 24 minutes.
Check this answer: 63 × 27 = 1,071. Show correct partial products.
63 × 20 = 1,260; 63 × 7 = 441; total 1,701. The final answer alone does not show which step was mistaken.
Which is reasonable for 296 x 18: 532, 5,328, or 53,280?
A theater has 36 rows of 128 seats.
Use a second method to check 214 x 32.
Explain why the second partial product shifts one place.
It represents multiplication by tens, not ones.

title: Rates and Percent Small-Group Lab
subject: Mathematics
standard: NC.6.RP.3 - Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, including unit rates and percentages.
source: North Carolina Department of Public Instruction, Mathematics Standards Vertical Progression: https://www.dpi.nc.gov/documents/publications/catalog/ma196-vertical-progression-math/open; NC Check-Ins 2.0 Mathematics Specifications: https://www.dpi.nc.gov/documents/accountability/testing/nc-checkin/nc-check-ins-20-mathematics-grades-3-8-specifications (accessed September 14, 2026).
focus: Use tables, unit rates, and percentages to compare situations and justify decisions.
qs: A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours. Unit rate?
A $40 item is discounted 15%. Discount amount?
A recipe uses 2 cups for 5 servings. Cups per serving?
Which is cheaper: 6 pens for $9 or 10 for $16?
A map scale is 1 inch:8 miles. 3.5 inches represents?
A runner completes 5 km in 25 min. Minutes per km?
Create a ratio table for 4 tickets costing $30.
A class of 24 has 18 present. Percent present?

title: Linear Models Homework and Exit Ticket
subject: Mathematics
standard: NC.8.F.4 - Analyze functions that model linear relationships; determine and interpret rate of change and initial value from two values or from a graph, table, or description.
source: North Carolina Department of Public Instruction, Mathematics Standards Vertical Progression: https://www.dpi.nc.gov/documents/publications/catalog/ma196-vertical-progression-math/open; NC Check-Ins 2.0 Mathematics Specifications: https://www.dpi.nc.gov/documents/accountability/testing/nc-checkin/nc-check-ins-20-mathematics-grades-3-8-specifications (accessed September 14, 2026).
focus: Build linear models from tables and contexts and interpret slope and initial value with units.
qs: Write y=mx+b when m=4 and b=-2.
Table: x 0,2,4; y 5,11,17. Find m and b.
A taxi charges $4 plus $2.50 per mile. Model.
Line through (3,10) with slope 2. Find b.
Same rate; first starts 6 units higher
A tank has 90 L and drains 6 L/min. Model.
From y values 8,13,18 as x rises by 1, find rate.
Answers vary; $30 start plus $12 per unit
State one limitation of a linear model.
Constant rate may not continue outside observed range.

title: French 101 Café Conversations
subject: French
standard: Course objective - Exchange basic greetings and cafe requests using polite expressions, articles, and present-tense forms of être and avoir.
source: Course objective; grammar reference: https://www.laits.utexas.edu/tex/index.html. Original practice; no affiliation.
focus: Use beginner French for greetings, identity, and simple cafe interactions.
qs: Complete with avoir: Nous ___ deux cafés.
Say: I would like a tea, please.
Je voudrais un thé, s’il vous plaît.
Choose article for croissant: un or une?
Reply: I am well, thank you.
Write an indefinite plural: un café.
Put in order: voudrais / je / de l’eau.
Answers vary; accurate greeting and response.
Must include greeting, request, response, and thanks.

title: German 101 Introductions Practice
subject: German
standard: Course objective - Introduce oneself and exchange basic personal information using greetings, pronouns, sein, heißen, and regular present-tense verbs.
source: Course-level learning objective; no accreditation, transfer, or universal equivalency claimed.
focus: Build accurate beginner introductions and short exchanges in German.
qs: Ask informally: What is your name?
Ask formally: Where are you from?
Answers vary; greeting and name required.
Must include greeting, two information exchanges, and closing.

title: Mandarin 101 Campus Basics
subject: Mandarin Chinese
standard: Course objective - Interpret basic greetings, name questions, identity sentences, and selected numbers using characters and tone-marked pinyin.
source: Course-level learning objective; no accreditation, transfer, or universal equivalency claimed.
focus: Practice respectful beginner exchanges with characters, pinyin, and English meaning.
qs: Hello. In speech, the first third tone changes before another third tone.
Thank you; the second syllable is neutral tone.
你叫什么名字？(Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?) asks what?
Translate: 我叫 Katia。(Wǒ jiào Katia.)
Write tone-marked pinyin for 再见.
Translate: 我是学生。(Wǒ shì xuésheng.)
Which pronoun means I/me: 我 (wǒ) or 你 (nǐ)?
Put in order: 叫 / 我 / Leonidas
Write: Nice to meet you. Include tone-marked pinyin.
很高兴认识你。Hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.
What does 是 (shì) do in the model 我是学生?
Links the subject to a noun identifying them. Do not insert 是 before every adjective.
Answers vary; accurate greeting and reply.
Write a four-line introduction with pinyin support.
Must include greeting, name question/answer, and closing.

title: ASL 101 Classroom Communication Reflection Guide
subject: American Sign Language
standard: Course objective - Explain visual-attention norms and reflect on fingerspelling and classroom exchanges after qualified live or video instruction.
source: Instructor-led prerequisite. ASL University reference: https://www.lifeprint.com/asl101/topics/parameters-asl.htm. No affiliation or endorsement.
focus: Reflect on visual communication, fingerspelling habits, and classroom interaction after an ASL lesson. This is a text-based companion, not an illustrated sign dictionary or standalone signing course.
qs: What should you establish before signing?
Name one respectful way to gain attention.
Wave within sight, tap shoulder lightly, or use room light with permission.
Why is mouthing every English word not ASL grammar?
ASL has its own grammar and nonmanual markers.
What is fingerspelling mainly used for?
Names, places, and terms without a known sign.
How should beginners fingerspell a name?
Smoothly at readable pace, not letter-by-letter punching.
What nonmanual signal commonly marks yes/no questions?
Raised eyebrows with appropriate body posture.
Where should hands stay for clear signing?
Comfortable signing space visible to partner.
Why avoid grabbing a Deaf signer for attention?
It is intrusive; use respectful visual/tactile norms.
A limited written notation for discussing signs, not ASL itself.
How can a partner request repetition?
Use an appropriate repeat/again request and puzzled facial expression.
It maintains attention and carries grammatical/social information.
Clear sightlines, adequate light, minimal visual obstruction.
Check hand position, rhythm, clarity, and eye gaze.
Short repeated practice with feedback from qualified sources.

title: Art Appreciation Composition Detective
subject: Fine Arts
standard: Course objective - Analyze how line, shape, color, value, texture, space, emphasis, balance, rhythm, and unity affect meaning in original compositions.
source: Original discussion and drawing prompts. Learners create two abstract sketches on separate paper; no artwork reproductions or ready-made composition studies are included.
focus: Use art vocabulary to compare and revise two abstract sketches you create: one calm composition and one crowded or tense composition.
qs: A focal area given greater visual attention.
A strong difference isolates or highlights an element.
Shape is two-dimensional; form appears or is three-dimensional.
Light-dark shifts can suggest volume and distance.
Visual weight mirrors across an axis.
How can warm colors affect focus?
They may appear to advance and attract attention.
Choose two elements to show calm.
Answers vary; e.g., horizontal lines and low contrast.
Choose two elements to show tension.
Answers vary; e.g., diagonals and sharp contrast.
Parts feel intentionally related as a whole.
Increase negative space and strengthen hierarchy.
Must name evidence and explain effect.
Observation states visible facts; interpretation explains possible meaning.

title: Introduction to Engineering Design Challenge
subject: Engineering / CTE
standard: Course objective - Define a design problem, distinguish criteria from constraints, generate and compare concepts, plan a fair test, and justify an evidence-based iteration.
source: Course-level learning objective; no accreditation, transfer, or universal equivalency claimed.
focus: Design a paper structure using at most 10 sheets, supporting 500 g for 10 seconds on a low tabletop. Record three trials, inspect failures, and justify one redesign. Use small classroom-safe weights under instructor supervision.
qs: A desired feature or measure of success.
A limit the design must obey.
Given max 10 sheets, identify the constraint.
Given support 500 g, identify the criterion.
Name a fair-test variable to control.
Same load placement, materials, span, or test time.
A testable representation of a design idea.
It reveals where and how to improve the design.
Create a weighted decision matrix with three criteria.
Answers vary; criteria, weights, scores, totals required.
Accuracy is closeness to true value; precision is repeatability.
Keep loads low, protect hands/eyes, and clear the test area.
They resist shape change and distribute loads.
State a testable claim about folded paper.
Answers vary; must identify design change and measurable outcome.
Use evidence to justify an iteration.
Cite test result, failure mode, and planned change.
Explain how improving one criterion may reduce another.
